title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Homeowner (EE1) shares personal data (e.g., name, address, email) with the Home Hub (P1) using a unique identifier (e.g., a unique user ID or account number). This allows the Home Hub to link the data to the specific individual, enabling profiling and identification.
assumptions: The data collected by the Homeowner is personal data containing unique identifiers.

title: Identifying Information via Identifier
description: The Homeowner shares data that contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (e.g., a unique user ID). This directly identifies the individual.
assumptions: The data shared by the Homeowner is identifiable information.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Homeowner shares personal data of a highly sensitive nature (e.g., health data, biometric data) with the Home Hub. This data type is collected and processed more frequently than functionally required, increasing the risk of misuse.
assumptions: The data shared is classified as highly sensitive personal data.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The Homeowner shares a large volume of personal data (e.g., a full profile of cameras and sensors) with the Home Hub. This exceeds the functional requirement of just registering the account.
assumptions: The data volume is excessive for the stated functional goal.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The Homeowner's consent to share data with the Home Hub may be invalid or insufficient, as the Home Hub may not be a pre-defined, trusted party, or the consent may be obtained under unclear conditions.
assumptions: The consent obtained by the Homeowner is not valid or lawful.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Homeowner may not be aware that their personal data is being shared with the Home Hub for the purpose of registering accounts and enrolling cameras/sensors.
assumptions: The Homeowner is unaware of the specific purpose of the data sharing.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: Guest User (EE2) shares a unique identifier (e.g., email, phone number) with the Home Hub (P1) to unlock the door. This identifier is globally unique and can be used to link the Guest to the Home Hub, enabling the Hub to identify the Guest's identity.
assumptions: The Guest User has a unique identifier that is known or discoverable by the Home Hub.

title: Identifiable Information via Identifier
description: The Guest User (EE2) provides identifiable information (e.g., a unique identifier) to the Home Hub (P1). This information is processed by the Hub, allowing the Hub to identify the Guest's identity.
assumptions: The identifier provided by the Guest is unique and sufficient to identify the Guest.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Guest User (EE2) shares personal data (e.g., email, phone number) with the Home Hub (P1). This data is highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required, but it is being shared unnecessarily for the purpose of unlocking a door.
assumptions: The data type (e.g., email) is considered highly sensitive and should not be shared for this purpose.

title: Lawful Processing of Personal Data
description: The Guest User (EE2) processes personal data (e.g., email) in a way that may not be lawful. Sharing personal data for the purpose of unlocking a door may not have a valid legal basis, such as valid consent or a legitimate interest.
assumptions: The Guest User does not have valid consent or a legitimate legal basis for sharing this personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the Home Hub uses a unique identifier (e.g., a specific sensor ID, device fingerprint, or unique event code) to identify the data subject, this creates a direct link between the data and the individual. This is a genuine threat because the data flow explicitly involves writing events to a log, and if the identifier is unique to the subject, the data is effectively linked to the individual.
assumptions: The Home Hub uses a unique identifier to identify the data subject.

title: Processing of Identified Information

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares camera clips using a unique identifier (e.g., camera ID, user ID) to link the data to a specific individual. This allows the Cloud Video Storage (DS2) to potentially identify the data subject.
assumptions: The camera clips contain a unique identifier that is not removed or obfuscated before sharing.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares personal data (camera clips) of a specific individual. The data type is highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required, but it is shared without explicit consent or a clear functional necessity.
assumptions: The camera clips contain personal data that is not functionally required for the video storage system.

title: Excessive Exposure to Predetermined Parties
description: The Cloud Video Storage (DS2) receives the camera clips and makes them accessible to a predetermined set of parties (e.g., the Home Hub, internal management, or third-party services) without a dynamic, consent-based, or narrowly scoped sharing mechanism. This amplifies the risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The data is stored and made available to a broad set of parties beyond what is strictly necessary for the video storage function.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or motion event ID). This allows the backend to link the alert to a specific individual or device, enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The motion alert contains a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the identifier is unique as stated in the threat-tree node L.1.1.

title: Identifying via Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert using an identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID) that uniquely identifies the data subject. This allows the mobile app backend to identify the specific individual receiving the alert.
assumptions: The identifier used is a unique reference to the data subject.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the identifier is a unique reference as stated in the threat-tree node I.2.1.1.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub forwards personal data (motion alert) to the mobile app backend. The alert may contain sensitive personal data (e.g., health, location, or behavioral data) that is processed beyond what is strictly functionally required for the basic forwarding.
assumptions: The motion alert contains sensitive personal data types.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert contains sensitive personal data as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.1.1.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend. The volume of personal data (the alert itself) is processed beyond what is functionally needed for the basic forwarding operation.
assumptions: The alert volume is excessive for the forwarding function.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert volume is excessive as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.2.1.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert to the mobile app backend. The processing and treatment of the personal data (the alert) is not necessary to achieve the functional goal of simply forwarding the data.
assumptions: The alert processing is not functionally necessary for the forwarding.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert processing is not functionally necessary as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.3.1.

title: Involved Parties
description: The Home Hub forwards personal data (motion alert) to the mobile app backend. The set of parties with whom the data is shared (Home Hub and Mobile App Backend) is known and static, but the data is shared with a party (the backend) that may not be functionally necessary for the alert's purpose.
assumptions: The backend is a known party, but the sharing is not strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the backend is a known party as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.4.1.1.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert to the mobile app backend without the data subject (user) being aware of this processing activity. The user may not know that their motion alert is being forwarded to a third party.
assumptions: The user is not aware of the forwarding of their motion alert.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the user is not aware of the forwarding as stated in the threat-tree node U.1.1.

title: Lawful Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards personal data (motion alert) to the mobile app backend. The processing of this data may not be lawful, for example, if the consent for processing the alert is invalid, missing, or not obtained.
assumptions: The processing of the alert is not lawful.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the processing is not lawful as stated in the threat-tree node Nc.1.1.3.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains a unique identifier (e.g., a user ID or device ID) that links the data to a specific individual. This allows the backend to link the notification to the specific homeowner, enabling identification.
assumptions: The notification includes a unique identifier.

title: Identifiable Information via Identifier
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains a unique identifier (e.g., a user ID or device ID) that identifies the data subject. This information is processed by the backend, allowing the homeowner to be singled out.
assumptions: The notification includes a unique identifier.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains personal data (motion-detected data) which is highly sensitive. This data is processed and transmitted to the external entity (homeowner) without sufficient justification for its collection and transmission.
assumptions: The notification contains sensitive personal data.

title: Lawful Processing of Personal Data
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains personal data (motion-detected data) which is highly sensitive. This data is processed and transmitted to the external entity (homeowner) without a valid legal basis (e.g., consent, legal obligation) for its collection and transmission.
assumptions: The notification contains sensitive personal data.

title: Observed Communications
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification is transmitted as a communication. The transmission of the notification (the data flow) is observed by the homeowner's phone, which may detect the presence of the notification and potentially link it to the user's identity.
assumptions: The notification is transmitted as a communication.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification is received by the homeowner's phone. The homeowner may not be aware that their personal data (motion-detected data) is being processed, stored, or transmitted by the backend.
assumptions: The homeowner is unaware of the processing of their personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor. The analytics data contains unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, user IDs) that allow the vendor to link and identify the specific individuals whose data is being shared.
assumptions: The analytics data includes unique identifiers that are not stripped or obfuscated before sharing.

title: Excessive Exposure to Predetermined Parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) receives the aggregated device-usage analytics. The vendor is a predetermined external party that is known and anticipated at design time. The data is shared with this specific vendor, which amplifies the potential risk of data exposure compared to sharing with a broad, dynamic set of parties.
assumptions: The vendor is a known, static party in the data sharing relationship.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend retrieves a stored video clip using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or video hash) from the data store. This identifier allows the backend to link the data to a specific individual, enabling the creation of a profile or association with other data.
assumptions: The video clip contains a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique within the system.

title: Linking via Quasi-identifier
description: The data flow transmits metadata about the parties involved in the retrieval process. This metadata may include information about the mobile app's identity, the homeowner's identity, or the video's content hash, which can be used to link the data flow to specific individuals.
assumptions: The metadata transmitted during the data flow contains identifying information about the parties.

title: Profiling via Association
description: The mobile app backend processes the retrieved video clip in the context of the homeowner's profile. By combining the video data with other stored data (e.g., user preferences, location history), the backend can infer the homeowner's identity or behavior patterns, effectively profiling the individual.
assumptions: The backend has access to the homeowner's profile data and performs association analysis on the video clip.
